vsPreviousWindow.note: The +28% is an artefact of WHICH DAYS fell in the window, not a regression that is still live. Within W44 the trend is monotonically DOWNWARD: 380 -> 421 -> 365 -> 304 -> 277 -> 277. By Fri/Sat the medians (277) are BELOW W43's weekly aggregate (291). The elevated numbers are concentrated on Mon 10-20 and Tue 10-21, the two highest-load weekdays at the start of a release push. Do NOT chase this as a code regression next week; compare 10-23..10-25 against W45's Mon/Tue instead.

sustainedShiftScan.method: Dense-day perceived max/min = 421/304 = 1.38, below the 1.5x bar over 3+ days. Including thin days it is 421/277 = 1.52 but that is a 2-day tail, not a sustained shift, and it points DOWNWARD. Worker FIPS 'run tests' step dense-day ratio = 311/203 = 1.53 but it is a single Tue 10-21 spike (242/311/225/203), not 3+ days. No step crossed the bar for 3+ consecutive days.

slowdownAttribution.verdict: shared-runner throughput / weekday-peak, not a code or cache regression
evidence: runnerWait is 5-11s all week, so queueing for a runner is not it; the time is inside the steps.
'install dependencies' is flat at 2-4s every day (22s only on 10-24) and Turbo remote-cache setup is ~0s, so cache coldness is NOT the driver.

The decline from Mon to Sat is uniform across unrelated jobs: web run tests 119->90 (-24%), worker run tests 120->94 (-22%), web FIPS 278->190 (-32%), worker FIPS 242->181 (-25%), e2e-tests job 253->151 (-40%). A code regression would not move five independent jobs by the same proportion.
Pearson r(concurrency@T+60s, perceived) = 0.314 and r(concurrency, gated) = 0.322 — weak-moderate, so concurrency explains part but not all.

Counter-evidence worth keeping: 10-23 had the week's HIGHEST total run volume (424 pipeline runs created) yet a LOWER median (304) than 10-20 (252 runs, 380). Raw run count is not the predictor; time-of-day burst shape is.

fipsBreakage.mechanism: The bump replaced Red Hat's nodejs RPM in worker/Dockerfile's UBI base stage with the upstream node:24.22.1-bookworm-slim binary, copied in via COPY --from=node /usr/local/bin/node /usr/bin/node. The RPM Node links the SYSTEM OpenSSL and therefore honours OPENSSL_FORCE_FIPS_MODE=1; upstream Node statically bundles its own non-validated, non-FIPS OpenSSL. So require('node:crypto').getFips() now returns 0 and the guard at scripts/ci/fips-tests.sh:28-31 exits 1 before a single test runs.
fipsBreakage.selfIncriminating: The commit ADDS the comment 'Cloud override: upstream Node 24.22.1 supplies full ICU and non-FIPS OpenSSL.' directly above the stage, and the pre-existing worker/Dockerfile header already warned 'Upstream node images statically bundle their own non-validated OpenSSL and bypass the platform module entirely.'
fipsBreakage.logEvidence: job 121212441171: 'The OpenSSL FIPS provider is not active; run with OPENSSL_FORCE_FIPS_MODE=1.' then '##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.'
fipsBreakage.blastRadius: 100% of runs since the bump fail tests-fips (web) and tests-fips (worker). Confirmed on the push run for current main HEAD 0e024ca8e (run 40225630874): those two jobs are the ONLY failing jobs out of 30. Because tests-fips is non-gating, nothing is blocked — FIPS coverage has been silently zero since 10-25 while the two jobs, which own the critical path in 71% of runs, still burn 145-175s of wall clock each on every run and stamp every run red.
fipsBreakage.whyNoDiff: Fixing this means editing worker/Dockerfile, which cannot be verified in this sandbox (no docker build, no node_modules, no pnpm). Per the standing rule, no diff is proposed for something whose checks could not be run. Reported for a human instead.
fipsBreakage.history: f964009483 previously reverted 'feat(docker): build FIPS images on Iron Bank Alpine instead of UBI 9 (#18449)' for a related toolchain reason. This is the second time the FIPS toolchain has been broken by a base-image change.
